messages.author: 39c444446d03805e
messages.subject: Fitting Linear Mixed Model for Clustered data
parts:
Hello,

I was trying to fit a linear mixed model where there is a random intercept for each cluster. I wanted to parameterize this model in a particular way. I wanted to define the within cluster variance using a broad, non-informative proper prior like Uniform[0, 10^4] and then specify a Beta(1.5, 10) prior for the Intra Class Correlation. 

The model is simple Y|X = \beta_0 + \beta_1 Treatment + Cluster + Individual_Error

I'm not sure if this is possible. I see that I can define the precision of the random effect, but I don't want to place a prior on that parameter. I want to link the within and between variances through the ICC, but only specify the within variance. 

Respectfully,
Zach

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting Linear Mixed Model for Clustered data
parts:
There is way to define your own joint prior for all hyperparmeters, and the
attached example shows how to use it.

even if you parameters that are log(precisions), for example, you can define a
new parameterisation, like

theta.new[1] = exp(-logprec1]) / (exp(-logprec1]) + exp(-logprec2]))

for the `correlation', and then

theta.new[2] = exp(-logprec1]) + exp(-logprec2])

for the sum of variances. then return the log-prior for theta.new[1:2] in the
logprec1:2] parametersisation. Then you also need the log(det(Jacobian)), where

jacobian package:numDeriv R Documentation

Gradient of a Vector Valued Function

Description:

Calculate the m by n numerical approximation of the gradient of a
real m-vector valued function with n-vector argument.

Usage:

jacobian(func, x, method="Richardson", side=NULL, method.args=list(),
...)


comes in handy.

please check on a simple example that you get it right...


please note that the output is still in the logprec parameterisation, but you
can use `inla.hyperpar.sample` to map them into yours.

Best
Havard
